info.bio:
Lush (1988 – 1996) fue una de las bandas más representativas del llamado movimiento Shoegaze, nacido a principios de los 90’ en el Reino Unido, junto con My bloody Valentine, Ride y Slowdive.

La banda estaba formada en un principio por Steve Rippon, Emma Anderson, Meriel Barham, Chris Acland y Miki Berenyi. Barham abandonó el grupo al poco tiempo, pero desde entonces la formación se mantuvo inalterable, hasta su desaparición.

Una de las características más relevantes de la música de Lush

scenes.name: Psicodelia británica de los noventa
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La edad de oro de la psicodelia británica no fueron los sesenta sino los noventa: las raves crean una demanda inagotable de música inducida por (o para) las drogas. La versión pop (Telescopes, Inspiral Carpets, Verve, Sundial, Auteurs, Kula Shaker), las más sofisticadas (Curve, Cranberries, Rollerskate Skinny, Beta Band, dEUS, Gorky's Zygotic Mynci), el space-rock libre (Porcupine Tree, Terminal Cheesecake, Heads), los últimos shoegazers (Ride, Swervedriver, Spectrum y E.A.R. de Sonic Boom, Spiritualized de Jason Pierce, Flying Saucer Attack, encuentro de shoegazing y ambient) y el dream-pop (Lush, Pale Saints, Slowdive, Catherine Wheel, Bark Psychosis).

podcast.title: Lollapalooza 1992 Appearance
podcast.body: The band was part of the "legendary mainstream lineup" for the 1992 Lollapalooza Festival, which also featured The Jesus and Mary Chain. This appearance highlighted their prominence within the alternative music scene of the early 1990s. "They toured with ride and were part of the legendary mainstream lineup for the 1992 Law of Paloose Festival, which by the way, also featured the Jesus and Marychain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Lollapalooza 1992 Appearance
podcast.body: Lush, described as an "up and coming shoot-ass band from the UK," was the first band on the main stage lineup for the second Lollapalooza tour, which began on July 18, 1992. "The first band was lush, an up and coming shoot-ass band from the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 90s Alt-Rock Discovery
podcast.body: Lush is listed as one of many bands from the 1990s that older listeners (e.g., in their mid-40s) who loved grunge as teenagers might discover as "new to them" music today. This suggests they were part of the broader alternative rock scene that went unnoticed by some at the time.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What A Drag It Is Getting Old (Musically)

podcast.title: Female-Led Band Dynamics
podcast.body: Lush, a London-based band composed of two men and two women, was notable for its "sexual equality," with the women, Miki Berenyi and Emma Anderson, largely "in charge" and responsible for writing "pretty much all the songs." This balance of female vocals with male guitar aggression was a notable aspect of the shoegaze scene. "Mickey Burrani and Emma Anderson, they were out front and wrote pretty much all the songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Genre Blending
podcast.body: The band's music is noted for blending elements of both shoegaze and dreampop, making it possible for individual songs to be categorized in either genre depending on critical interpretation. "my blood y balanta y en action sugar y hacia dreampop, pues yo creo que hacían los dos, dependiendo del diario, dependiendo de la canción podemos meterla en un lado."

srcs.episode: DREAM POP y SHOEGAZE. Diferencias entre ellos.

podcast.title: Outskirts of Britpop
podcast.body: Lush was identified as one of the "shoe-gazer bands" circling the outskirts of the Britpop universe, indicating their concurrent but distinct musical style during the era. "Circling the outskirts of this universe were shoe-gazer bands like My Bloody Valentine and Ride and Lush and Swerve Driver and Slow Dive."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock: Chapter 12

podcast.title: Pioneer of Shoegaze
podcast.body: Lush was one of the bands that emerged between 1989 and 1991, taking the combination of ethereal melody and distorted guitars further, following the blueprint laid out by My Bloody Valentine within the nascent Shoegaze scene. "En seguida, susguieron bandas como Ride, Slowdive, Feltzaint y Lash, quienes tomaron aquella combinación de melodía setéria, guitarras distorsionadas y la llevaron aún más lejos."

srcs.episode: El disco imposible: La historia de Loveless y My Bloody Valentine

podcast.title: Post-Band Careers
podcast.body: After Lush disbanded, singer Miki Berenyi became a production editor for British music magazines. Co-singer Emma Anderson transitioned into music business management, while bassist Phil King, after a stint playing bass in The Jesus and Mary Chain, began working in music media as a picture researcher. "Singer Mickey Burrani ended up as a production editor to a couple of British music magazines, and co-singer Emma Anderson works in music business management. And after a stint playing bass in the Jesus and Marychain, bassist Phil King works in music media as a picture researcher."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Shoegaze Band Example
podcast.body: Lush was mentioned as an example of a Shoegaze band, a genre that despite being pushed aside by Grunge in the early 90s, never truly went away and whose influences can still be felt in later bands. "There were bands like Slow Dive, Chapter House, Curve, Lush, My Bloody Valentine, Adorable, The Catherine Wheel."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tragic End and Aftermath
podcast.body: The band continued until 1996, at which point drummer Chris Acland committed suicide. Following this tragedy, the remaining members attempted to carry on but ultimately felt they "just couldn't," leading to the band's dissolution. "They lasted until 1996 when drummer Chris Acklin committed suicide. The band tried to carry on, but they felt they just couldn't."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
